doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bobby Danzig and Adam Lambert's Six Brown Cats
summary: Danzig as an early St. Louis follower of Dizzy; Terry does not know Lambert's band.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Someone that’s mentioned in Miles’s book, but I don’t know whether you’ve – actually, all the books on Miles: Bobby Danzig, trumpet player?

Bobby Danzig was a beautiful little player. He played a lot like what you would call the modern, advanced-type trumpet players, like Dizzy [Gillespie]. Bobby Danzig was one of the first people around St. Louis that we heard that was following Dizzy’s pattern. He – the last thing I heard from Bobby, he – I don’t know whether he was a diabetic or not, but he was an amputee. I think I heard he was a double amputee, and I don’t know whether he’s still around or what. But he was a marvelous trumpet player.
A band with an intriguing name to me: Adam Lambert’s Six Brown Cats.
That one I don’t know. Adam – I never heard that one.
Is that a St. Louis band?
